messages:
Sam Torres: FYI — after pushing the new ratecap rules ~15:40 UTC, a subset of customers started hitting 429s and increased p50 latency. Seeing reports from EU region first. Anyone on this rollout?
Maria Chen: I rolled the canary to 10% at 15:35. Noted alerts at 15:42. Quick snapshot: spike in 429s for endpoints /v1/generate and /v1/chat-stream.
Lee Patel: Logs show quota_check failures with auth token passing but policy eval timeout. Sample log: `policy_eval took=1202ms result=timeout user=acct-845`
Sam Torres: That aligns with what support is seeing — customer reported intermittent 502 then 429s. They included curl output: `HTTP/1.1 429 \nRetry-After: 30`
Maria Chen: Repro steps I used:
```
# reproduce: run 100 concurrent requests with user token
ab -n 500 -c 100 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
At 15:43 the canary pods started returning 429s while main pool stayed healthy.
Jordan R: OpsBot just posted the rollout change event: `deploy-service ratecap-v2 canary=10% user=platform@redwood`
Lee Patel: My hypothesis: new policy evaluation logic increased p99 policy latency, causing local rate limiter to count requests as violations when backend policy timed out. Need to confirm policy service latency traces.
Sam Torres: Priority: confirm blast radius and either pause canary or rollback. Support has 3 customers complaining — two on Dedicated (EU) and one Hosted.
Maria Chen: I recommend pausing canary immediate and draining canary routing — plan: 1) pause rollout 2) shift traffic back 3) monitor 429/latency 4) gather traces for policy service for 15:30-15:50 window. Who can execute?
Lee Patel: I can pause the rollout and route canary traffic off. CLI: `infractl rollout pause ratecap-v2 --canary` then `infractl traffic shift ratecap-v2 --from=canary --to=stable --percent=100 --grace=30s`
Jordan R: Executing now. `infractl rollout pause ratecap-v2 --canary` -> OpsBot: acknowledged.
OpsBot: rollout ratecap-v2 canary paused by jordan.r at 15:47 UTC.
Sam Torres: Good. After shift, support will ask customers for timestamps and sample request ids. Can we add a short-term mitigation (increase retry window) to reduce 429 chatter?
Maria Chen: We can temporarily relax the local limiter threshold for EU region. Patch: set `burst_limit_factor=1.5` in rate-limiter config and reload. I can coordinate a quick config push if we decide.
Lee Patel: Hold on config push until we confirm traces. If policy service is timing out we should also look at scaling it. Asking infra-metrics: `k8s top` shows policy-service replicas=2 p95 CPU=85%.
Jordan R: After traffic shift completed at 15:49:12, OpsBot shows canary pods drained. Early metrics: 429s dropped by ~80% within 2m.
OpsBot: traffic shift complete. canary=0% stable=100% at 15:51 UTC.
Sam Torres: Perfect. Support to customers: we'll follow up with postmortem and timeline. Action items: Maria collect policy traces; Lee check policy-service autoscale config; Jordan confirm dedicated customers saw rollback take effect; Sam draft customer-facing note.
Maria Chen: I pulled traces: a large GC pause on policy-1 at 15:40 caused policy_eval spikes. Trace IDs: trace-9a7c, trace-9a8d. Uploading to S3.
Lee Patel: Proposal for next steps before re-roll: add a soft timeout fallback in rate limiter (if policy eval >600ms, allow best-effort instead of hard 429) and increase policy-service horizontal autoscale to min 3 replicas.
Sam Torres: Sounds good. We'll keep the rollout paused. Jordan, can you open a PR for the autoscale tweak and a short patch for limiter fallback? Tag me and Maria for review.
Jordan R: Will do. PR templates: `infra/ratecap/autoscale.md` + `services/policy/fallback.md`. Target hotfix branch and coordinate with security review if needed.
Sam Torres: Thanks team. I'll update the customers that we've paused the rollout, are investigating GC and scaling, and will provide a timeline for a safe re-roll. :white_check_mark:
Maria Chen: Adding notes to the incident doc and linking traces.
Lee Patel: Follow-up: add a preflight smoke test for canary that includes a policy-eval latency check (p95 < 200ms) before routing production traffic.
Sam Torres: Agreed — let's include that in the runbook. Closing the thread for now, will re-open when we have rollback postmortem draft. :v:
